sources.title: National Park Service, Wales Sites National Historic Landmark
sources.note: NPS one-page landmark brief checked for the two archaeological sites, occupation since at least 500 CE, Birnirk artifacts, Kiŋigin and Kingikmiut names, and the approximately 68-mile umiak crossing.

sources.title: Smithsonian Institution, Walakpa Site, Alaska: Its Place in the Birnirk and Thule Cultures
sources.note: Smithsonian monograph checked at printed pages 1 to 8 and 96 to 104 for terminology, chronology, Walakpa, Point Hope, and Kotzebue comparisons.

sources.title: National Park Service, Capturing History in the Beach Ridges of Cape Krusenstern
sources.note: NPS interpretation checked for Western Thule and Kotzebue archaeological periods, semi-subterranean houses, building materials, and changing house form.

sources.title: National Park Service, How the Arctic coast and culture intertwined
sources.note: NPS research summary checked for preservation limits, settlement density, environmental change, and an increase until about five hundred years ago.

sources.title: Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports, archaeobotany of an early Thule Iñupiaq dwelling
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study checked in sections 3 to 5 for a late thirteenth- to mid-fourteenth-century Cape Espenberg house, plant contexts, midden, roof, and formation-process cautions.

sources.title: National Park Service, Alaska Natives and Early People
sources.note: NPS regional history checked for seasonal mobility, resource availability, and the documented danger of outsiders mistaking a seasonal shortage for chronic starvation.

sources.title: Alaska Eskimo Whaling Commission, Our Villages
sources.note: Community organization page checked for eleven whaling communities, Iñupiat and Siberian Yupik distinction, marine and terrestrial foods, sharing, and village variation.

sources.title: Alaska Eskimo Whaling Commission, Our Story and Mission
sources.note: Community organization page checked for Iñupiat and Siberian Yupik membership, long whaling continuity, adaptation, co-management, and present cultural responsibility.

sources.title: Alaska Eskimo Whaling Commission, Nalukataq
sources.note: Community organization page checked for whole-community participation, meat and maktak sharing, future generations, and contemporary feast timing.

sources.title: Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Bowhead Subsistence Hunt Environmental Impact Statement
sources.note: Government report checked at PDF pages 25 to 31, section 1.1.4, for community-wide effort, captains, crews, knowledge, food, and formalized sharing.

sources.title: Iñupiat Community of the Arctic Slope, Communities
sources.note: Tribal government page checked for the eight distinct North Slope communities, their varied landscapes and practices, and the modern organization’s geographic scope.

sources.title: Iñupiat Community of the Arctic Slope, Comprehensive Economic Development Strategy 2025-2030
sources.note: Tribal government plan checked at PDF pages 6 to 8 for family and kinship, elders, children, language, sharing, cooperation, humor, health, and cultural values.

sources.title: Iñupiat Community of the Arctic Slope, Education
sources.note: Tribal education page checked for present language- and culture-rooted education, Qargi Academy, apprenticeships, community partnerships, and services across ages.

sources.title: North Slope Borough Iñupiat Heritage Center, Language
sources.note: Community institution page checked for its exact modern Iñupiatun greeting and English translation, language programs, and learning resources.

sources.title: University of Alaska Fairbanks, Edna MacLean North Slope Iñupiaq lexicon
sources.note: University project page checked for four dialect types in two groups, named community contributors, elder verification, and dictionary scale.

sources.title: Kawerak, Indigenous Knowledge and Use of Bering Strait Region Ocean Currents
sources.note: Community-reviewed book checked at PDF pages 5 to 12 and 27 to 29 for currents, ice, animals, safety, place-specific expertise, youth learning, and review by tribes and local experts.

sources.title: North Slope Borough, Iñupiat History, Language and Culture budget narrative
sources.note: Borough document checked at PDF pages G-2 to G-5 for Traditional Land Use Inventory work, oral histories, artifacts, education, elders, youth, and Nunamiut museum responsibilities.

sources.title: Smithsonian Ocean, Iñupiat Ceremonial Mask
sources.note: Smithsonian object page checked for spruce, caribou teeth, thanksgiving ceremony, and breastplate images of whaling crews in umiaks.

sources.title: Smithsonian Center for Folklife and Cultural Heritage, Native Dolls educational guide
sources.note: Smithsonian guide checked at PDF pages 11 to 13 for an Iñupiat doll maker, girls practicing parka sewing, layered caribou clothing, large hoods, and gut waterproofing.

sources.title: Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium, Water and Sanitation
sources.note: Tribal health page checked in the Kivalina PASS and Water and Wellness sections for present water sources, sinks, toilets, waste separation, honey buckets, hygiene, and explicit modern infrastructure.

sources.title: Smithsonian Institution, Ethnological Results of the Point Barrow Expedition
sources.note: Public-domain 1893 colonial ethnography checked at printed pages 70 to 75, 418 to 423, and 427 to 428 for houses, adoption, household authority, hygiene, waste, and healing, with its observer and date limits retained.

sources.title: National Park Service, The Hope and Promise of Ublasaun: A Herder’s Story
sources.note: NPS community history checked for Shishmaref women healers and midwives, named kin, adoption, settlement layout, seasonal dispersal, houses, and twentieth-century change.

sources.title: ERIC, Paul Ongtooguk, Aspects of Traditional Inupiat Education
sources.note: ERIC full text checked at article pages 8 to 12 for observation, stories, apprenticeship, chores, environmental judgment, responsibility, and community as a place of learning.

sources.title: Alaska State Library, Iñupiat Eskimo Dictionary catalog record
sources.note: State library record checked for authorship, 1970 publication, University of Alaska rural-school preparation, Inupiaq language, and the distinction between a modern dictionary and a 1492 text.

sources.title: Alaska State Museums, Sheldon Jackson Museum permanent exhibits
sources.note: State museum page checked for separate Iñupiat and Yupik collection framing and uses of skin, gut, driftwood, ivory, bone, kayaks, clothing, baskets, and masks.

sources.title: National Park Service, Subsistence in the Arctic
sources.note: NPS page checked for present Point Hope whaling, community observations, intergenerational knowledge, sea ice, permafrost, and the need to label modern evidence as continuity.

sources.title: National Park Service, Alaska Park Science volume 16
sources.note: NPS journal checked in the Cape Krusenstern articles, especially PDF pages 19 to 31, for survey methods, features, beach-ridge chronology, preservation, and interpretation limits.

sources.title: Smithsonian Institution, Crossroads of Continents: Cultures of Siberia and Alaska exhibition
sources.note: Smithsonian exhibition record checked for its 1988 to 1989 dates, joint preparation, broad Alaska and Siberia scope, and listed kayaks, harpoons, ivory carvings, beadwork, drums, clothing, journals, photographs, and film.

sources.title: University of Alaska Fairbanks, About time: burial chronology at Ipiutak, Point Hope
sources.note: University thesis record checked for four burial types, remapping, taphonomy, accelerator dates, long site use, and limits on gender or status inference.

sources.title: Iñupiat Community of the Arctic Slope, Community Services
sources.note: Tribal government page checked for present elder respite and chore services, child and family support, scholarships, burial aid, and organizational scope.

sources.title: National Park Service, The Bering Land Bridge Theory
sources.note: NPS history checked for long cross-strait travel and trade known locally before eighteenth-century European mapping, plus the distinction between ancient migrations and later communities.

sources.title: National Park Service, Cape Krusenstern Coastal Settlement Patterns resource brief
sources.note: NPS one-page research brief checked for systematic survey, nearly continuous occupation over two millennia, environmental variability, and cautious resilience questions.
